system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Miami, United States. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Miami itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Miami space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Little Haiti/Little River, Allapattah, Wynwood, Design District, Downtown, Coral Gables, Miami Beach, Doral) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Miami spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Miami, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Fredric Snitzer Gallery
galleries.note: Miami’s most established internationally connected contemporary gallery, with a long Art Basel presence and an influential multigenerational roster.

galleries.name: Nina Johnson
galleries.note: A nationally prominent programme spanning emerging artists, major Miami figures and critically reappraised practices.

galleries.name: David Castillo
galleries.note: Internationally respected for conceptually rigorous exhibitions and strong advocacy for queer artists and artists of color.

galleries.name: Spinello Projects
galleries.note: A central force in Miami’s contemporary scene, known for ambitious installations and sustained support of locally rooted artists.

galleries.name: Locust Projects
galleries.note: Miami’s seminal alternative art space, commissioning experimental, site-specific projects since 1998.

galleries.name: Piero Atchugarry Gallery
galleries.note: An internationally active Miami–Uruguay gallery with a strong programme of sculpture, abstraction and Latin American conceptual art.

galleries.name: Central Fine
galleries.note: A critically followed gallery pairing emerging international artists with distinctive South Florida practices.

galleries.name: Jupiter Contemporary
galleries.note: A fast-rising gallery with notable fair participation and an adventurous programme focused on emerging global artists.

galleries.name: Pan American Art Projects
galleries.note: A longstanding authority on contemporary art from Cuba and the Americas, with substantial institutional and fair visibility.

galleries.name: Dot Fiftyone Gallery
galleries.note: An established platform for Latin American and international contemporary art, particularly conceptualism, photography and abstraction.

galleries.name: Emerson Dorsch
galleries.note: One of Miami’s formative contemporary galleries, with decades of support for experimental and locally influential artists.

galleries.name: Dimensions Variable
galleries.note: An artist-led nonprofit recognized for research-driven exhibitions, new commissions and experimental spatial practices.

galleries.name: KDR
galleries.note: A closely watched emerging gallery whose intergenerational programme has earned national press and major fair invitations.

galleries.name: Mindy Solomon Gallery
galleries.note: Known nationally for contemporary ceramics alongside painting, sculpture and materially adventurous interdisciplinary work.

galleries.name: The Bonnier Gallery
galleries.note: A focused programme connecting postwar minimal and conceptual art with exacting contemporary abstraction.

galleries.name: LnS Gallery
galleries.note: Represents important Cuban, Latin American and Miami artists through a polished programme with institutional reach.

galleries.name: Voloshyn Gallery
galleries.note: The Kyiv-founded gallery’s permanent Miami space brings internationally visible Ukrainian and Eastern European practices to the city.

galleries.name: Galería La Cometa
galleries.note: The Colombian gallery’s Miami branch adds a substantial Latin American programme and established international fair network.

galleries.name: El Apartamento
galleries.note: An influential Havana-founded gallery presenting Cuban and international artists through an independent, cross-border programme.

galleries.name: PRIMARY
galleries.note: An artist-founded gallery and cultural platform with deep roots in Miami’s street, design and contemporary-art communities.

galleries.name: Oolite Arts
galleries.note: A major artist-support organization whose galleries present curated exhibitions, commissions and work by resident artists.

galleries.name: Bakehouse Art Complex
galleries.note: A longstanding nonprofit studio complex with an increasingly ambitious public exhibition and commissioning programme.

galleries.name: Faena Art
galleries.note: Produces prominent public commissions, installations and project-room exhibitions with leading international contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Nohra Haime Gallery
galleries.note: A veteran international gallery presenting Latin American, European and US artists across painting, sculpture and installation.

galleries.name: ArtSpace/Virginia Miller Galleries
galleries.note: One of South Florida’s longest-running galleries, especially important for Latin American and Caribbean contemporary art.

galleries.name: Diana Lowenstein Gallery
galleries.note: A longstanding Miami gallery with an international programme and a history of ambitious installations and art-fair participation.

galleries.name: Gary Nader Art Centre
galleries.note: A major commercial force in Latin American modern and contemporary art, with extensive inventory and regional market influence.

galleries.name: Homework
galleries.note: An emerging gallery and creative platform cultivating young Miami and international artists through exhibitions and fairs.

galleries.name: Andrew Reed Gallery
galleries.note: A critically oriented young gallery showing emerging artists and participating in respected independent fairs.

galleries.name: Tomás Redrado Art
galleries.note: A young Latin American gallery building visibility for emerging artists through Miami exhibitions and international fairs.

galleries.name: Green Space Miami
galleries.note: A Green Family Foundation initiative presenting socially engaged exhibitions with strong local and diasporic perspectives.

galleries.name: Edge Zones
galleries.note: A durable experimental nonprofit supporting performance, video, installation and exchange across the Caribbean and Americas.

galleries.name: Bridge Red Studios/Project Space
galleries.note: An artist-run venue known for thoughtful exhibitions connecting established South Florida artists with younger practices.

galleries.name: Swampspace Gallery
galleries.note: One of Miami’s longest-lived artist-run spaces, valued for irreverent, experimental exhibitions and community history.

galleries.name: Laundromat Art Space
galleries.note: An artist-run studio and exhibition space that provides an accessible platform for emerging Miami practices.

galleries.name: IS Projects
galleries.note: A respected printmaking studio and gallery advancing artist books, editions and experimental works on paper.

galleries.name: The Contemporary Art Modern Project
galleries.note: Known as The CAMP Gallery, it foregrounds women, LGBTQ artists and diasporic contemporary practices.

galleries.name: Dále Zine
galleries.note: An artist-run publishing platform and exhibition venue central to Miami’s independent zine, edition and emerging-art ecosystem.

galleries.name: Durban Segnini Gallery
galleries.note: A longstanding specialist in Latin American abstraction, geometric art and related contemporary practices.

galleries.name: Ascaso Gallery
galleries.note: A Miami branch of the Venezuelan-founded gallery with substantial holdings and exhibitions in Latin American modern and contemporary art.

galleries.name: Cernuda Arte
galleries.note: An authoritative gallery for Cuban art, combining historical scholarship with representation of significant contemporary Cuban artists.

galleries.name: Art Nouveau Gallery
galleries.note: An established Venezuelan-founded gallery with a permanent Miami programme and regular international fair participation.

galleries.name: Fabien Castanier Gallery
galleries.note: An international gallery associated with urban contemporary art, large-scale painting and artists emerging from street-art contexts.

galleries.name: The Americas Collection
galleries.note: A veteran Coral Gables gallery with sustained expertise in modern and contemporary art from Latin America and the Caribbean.

galleries.name: Imago Art in Action
galleries.note: A nonprofit exhibition platform supporting contemporary Latin American artists, educational programmes and cultural exchange.

galleries.name: Opera Gallery Miami
galleries.note: The global gallery’s permanent Miami branch has considerable market reach across postwar, contemporary and secondary-market art.

galleries.name: Markowicz Fine Art
galleries.note: A high-traffic commercial gallery with an international network and a programme spanning pop, street art, photography and sculpture.

galleries.name: Oliver Cole Gallery
galleries.note: A Miami-based gallery presenting established and emerging international contemporary artists in a large exhibition space.

galleries.name: Taglialatella Galleries Miami
galleries.note: A permanent branch of the international dealer, focused on blue-chip pop art, editions and urban contemporary work.

galleries.name: Zadok Gallery
galleries.note: A longstanding Wynwood gallery presenting international contemporary painting, sculpture and installation.

galleries.name: Waltman Ortega Fine Art
galleries.note: A Miami–Paris gallery connecting European, Latin American and South Florida artists through exhibitions and fairs.

galleries.name: Sammer Gallery
galleries.note: An established specialist in Latin American geometric abstraction and its contemporary descendants.

galleries.name: Yeelen Gallery
galleries.note: An important Black-owned gallery that has advanced African-diasporic, Caribbean and socially engaged contemporary art in Miami.

galleries.name: IPC ArtSpace
galleries.note: A photography-centered space created by the Iris PhotoCollective, presenting documentary and fine-art projects with civic relevance.

galleries.name: Hampton Art Lovers at the Historic Ward Rooming House
galleries.note: A culturally important nonprofit gallery presenting Black art within one of historic Overtown’s landmark buildings.

galleries.name: KROMA Art Space & Studios
galleries.note: A community-rooted venue providing studios and exhibitions for artists from Coconut Grove and across Miami.

galleries.name: Goldman Global Arts Gallery
galleries.note: The commercial gallery associated with Wynwood Walls brings internationally known muralists and street artists into a gallery setting.

galleries.name: WYN 317 Gallery
galleries.note: A locally established platform for Miami street art, graffiti, pop-inflected work and emerging artists.

galleries.name: Mirus Gallery Miami
galleries.note: The Miami branch of a multcity gallery presenting contemporary figurative, surrealist and urban-influenced art.

galleries.name: Manolis Projects
galleries.note: A large independent gallery and studio venue giving Miami artists substantial space for exhibitions and public events.

galleries.name: Collective 62
galleries.note: An artist-run collective that supports shared studios, collaborative exhibitions and neighborhood-based cultural activity.

galleries.name: New Low
galleries.note: A small artist-run venue valued for experimental exhibitions by emerging local and visiting artists.

galleries.name: Good To Know.FYI
galleries.note: An independent project space contributing intimate, artist-led exhibitions and events to Little River’s contemporary-art ecology.
